projects.title: The Last Promise
projects.brief: After her fiancé steals her company, a young founder enters a marriage of convenience with his greatest rival. A hidden recording could change everything.

projects.title: Velvet Lies
projects.brief: A hotel pianist recognizes a powerful guest as the man who vanished from her life. His new identity hides a dangerous family secret.

projects.title: A Second Chance
projects.brief: Two former lovers inherit a failing coastal bookstore. They have thirty days to save it and face the letter that kept them apart.

projects.title: Crown of Ashes
projects.brief: An overlooked heiress returns to reclaim her family's publishing empire, with help from the one person she was taught never to trust.

projects.title: After Midnight
projects.brief: A late-night radio host receives messages from a stranger who knows the truth about her sister's disappearance.

projects.title: Wild Hearts
projects.brief: A city architect returns to her hometown to restore a theater, only to find her first love leading the campaign to tear it down.

issues.excerpt: I have never set foot in that boardroom, Clara said.
issues.cause: Clara led the acquisition meeting in episode 3. The generation step omitted this fact from the Story Bible.
issues.originalPrompt: Write the next episode. Keep the characters consistent.
issues.optimizedPrompt: Before writing, check every character claim against the Story Bible. Clara led the acquisition meeting in episode 3 and remembers the boardroom. Preserve her agency and cautious trust. Show emotion through dialogue and action; never contradict established events.
issues.replacement: I know that boardroom, Clara said. I know exactly where he was sitting when he signed my company away.

issues.excerpt: By morning, the recording was in her hands. She knew what she had to do.
issues.cause: The chapter jumps to the recording without establishing how Clara obtained it. The hook resolves tension instead of creating a new question.
issues.originalPrompt: Create a dramatic ending to this chapter.
issues.optimizedPrompt: Connect each scene to the previous outline. Show Clara obtaining the recording through a motivated decision with a real cost. End the chapter on a specific revelation or unresolved choice. Do not resolve the central conflict before the next episode.
issues.replacement: The night guard slid the recorder across the desk. Play the last ten seconds, he whispered. Then tell me if you still want to marry him.

issues.excerpt: As an AI language model, I can describe her emotions as a tapestry of complex feelings. 她很伤心.
issues.cause: Model self-disclosure, mixed-language output, and generic emotional description interrupt the English audio experience.
issues.optimizedPrompt: Tell the story like a real person calling a close friend. Use natural English dialogue to move the plot forward. Show feelings through choices, pauses, and concrete actions. Output only the episode script in English. Never mention AI, prompts, or the writing process; avoid repeated metaphors.
issues.replacement: He called three times. Clara watched the screen light up, then turned the phone face down. Not tonight, she said.

issues.excerpt: He replied quickly while she spoke across him and then the door opened and someone laughed.
issues.cause: Long sentences and missing speaker boundaries make turn-taking unclear in narration.
issues.optimizedPrompt: Use explicit speaker labels, short dialogue turns, and separate action beats. Insert a 300ms pause at speaker changes and a 700ms pause before the final reveal. Target 145–155 words per minute. Do not read production annotations aloud.
issues.replacement:
CLARA: You knew?
[Pause 300ms]
ADRIAN: I was trying to protect you.
[Door opens. Pause 700ms]
ELENA: Then you should have told her about me.

issues.excerpt: Nora smiled. She had never cared about books.
issues.cause: Nora's childhood love of the bookstore is established in the Story Bible but missing from the chapter context.
issues.optimizedPrompt: Preserve Nora's established love of the bookstore. Her resistance comes from the lost letter, not a dislike of books. Express hurt through a concrete memory and restrained dialogue.
issues.replacement: Nora ran a finger along the shelf. You kept my favorite book, she said. You kept everything except the letter.
